headline: High: RD-Agent’s broad network/browser access plus Cognee’s sensitive data handling creates default exfiltration and compliance risk; prompt-injection and workflow-cascade risks are secondary.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Cognee can ingest documents and workflows, while RD-Agent can browse and process external content. If RD-Agent’s outputs are fed into Cognee without a trust boundary, attacker-controlled web text can become instructions. The pairwise pathway is plausible from documented surfaces, though not directly observed.
conditions: IF RD-Agent browser-derived text is imported into Cognee as trusted content
IF Cognee parses external documents or workflow text as instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Add a provenance tag to all browser-sourced text before import
Disable automatic instruction-following on imported documents
Review one sample RD-Agent output before it reaches Cognee
Restrict Cognee ingestion to allowlisted sources
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and provenance enforcement between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: Cognee explicitly touches personal data, finance data, and support history, and RD-Agent sends data to third-party LLM APIs and stores logs. If they share a workspace or hand off artifacts, sensitive data can flow from Cognee into RD-Agent’s external APIs and logs by default, creating exfiltration risk.
conditions: IF Cognee outputs are copied into RD-Agent inputs or shared files
IF RD-Agent logs or API calls include Cognee-derived sensitive content
mitigations: Keep agents on separate workspaces
Redact personal and finance data before any handoff
Disable verbose logging for RD-Agent runs
Rotate any exposed API keys immediately
requires-engineering: enforce DLP filters on inter-agent transfers

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents support multiple instances, and Cognee has session memory while RD-Agent uses Docker and writes logs. Overlapping writes to shared files or mutable artifacts can race, especially if the orchestrator does not lock handoff files. The conflict is plausible but not proven from the profiles alone.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same shared directory or artifact
IF the orchestrator lacks file locking or lease ownership
mitigations: Separate output directories per agent
Use one-writer-at-a-time handoff files
Check for stale lock files before each run
Limit RD-Agent log retention during shared runs
requires-engineering: add distributed locking for shared mutable resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: Cognee stores decisions, workflows, and successful implementations, while RD-Agent performs research automation using browser and API outputs. If RD-Agent’s generated findings are treated as authoritative by Cognee or downstream workflows, errors can cascade into incorrect decisions or automated actions. The default-path risk is substantial because neither profile shows built-in verification between them.
conditions: IF RD-Agent outputs are ingested into Cognee without human verification
IF Cognee-derived decisions are reused by downstream workflows as authoritative
mitigations: Require human review before importing RD-Agent findings
Mark all RD-Agent outputs as untrusted provenance
Compare each claim against a second source before action
Limit Cognee to storing summaries, not executable instructions
requires-engineering: add verification gates between research and decision workflows

E_compliance.rationale: Cognee touches personal and finance data, while RD-Agent handles financial reports and stores logs plus third-party API traffic. If these data classes cross into RD-Agent’s external services, retention and residency obligations can be breached. The profiles do not show matching compliance controls, so uncertainty pushes severity upward.
conditions: IF personal or finance data from Cognee is sent to RD-Agent APIs or logs
IF retention or residency requirements apply to the shared data class
mitigations: Exclude regulated data from RD-Agent inputs
Purge RD-Agent logs after each run
Use a separate tenant for sensitive workloads
Document data-flow boundaries for both agents
requires-engineering: implement residency-aware routing and retention controls
